correctness.rationale: The standard unordered deleted-product complex on K6 has cellular dimensions (15,60,45) and verified d1 d2=0. A 24-by-24 determinant-one primitive cocycle-lattice certificate plus a 36-by-36 determinant-two minor prove rank 36. A 35-by-35 determinant-one minor and characteristic-two rank 35 force Smith factors 1 repeated 35 times and 2 once, giving integral \(H^2\cong\mathbb Z^9\oplus\mathbb Z/2\). A separate determinant-one complement minor of the 15 disjoint non-tree-edge square products establishes integral degree-two cup surjectivity. An explicit integer cochain identity shows twice the given five-term cup representative is a coboundary; exact characteristic-two rank growth proves it is not itself an integral coboundary. The standalone verify.py recomputes everything from graph edges using exact arithmetic. The claim is specific to the given finite graph; no unverified infinite extrapolation is made.

originality.rationale: The integer cup-product map on the collision-free unordered two-point configuration of K6, including the explicit order-two product, is more specific than published ordered complete-graph cohomology, general graph-braid first homology, and differently-coefficient homology results. Both published comparisons and semantic index results were checked at the level of coefficient rings, ordered/unordered spaces, graph parameter, and multiplicative versus additive conclusion. No source inspected was seen to determine this precise integral ring-generation statement. This is a best-knowledge priority assessment, not a proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: An unindexed computation of the full unordered K6 cup product, or a theorem with hidden equivalent consequences, could supersede the finding.
The Ramos–Yun 2026 full text was unavailable, so the comparison rests on its abstract; its stated rational theme makes an integral two-torsion implication unlikely but not impossible.
Only abstract-level inspection of Ko–Park was performed; its first-homology topic is insufficient by itself for an integral cup-product conclusion.

value.rationale: The six-vertex complete graph is a smallest canonical complete-graph case with nontrivial second rational homology for unordered two-point configurations, beyond the classical K5 nonorientable surface model. The determination that all integral cohomology, INCLUDING the naturally arising \(\mathbb Z/2\) class, is generated by degree-one motions resolves a meaningful multiplicative gap left by additive and ordered-cover results. The explicit order-two cup representative probes topology lost under rationalization, and is a directly reusable low-dimensional benchmark for graph-braid cohomology. A narrow natural exact invariant with a non-implied answer suffices; the claim makes no unsupported classification or downstream promises.
